first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent me this because she's leaning towards Crete. The first paragraph says the packages share a name and almost nothing else, and that rooms and the reception are where they differ. That's where our money goes, so I'll read it properly, start to finish, with a cup of tea.

journey.quote: A venue package, a venue fee and a planner each cover different ground, so check who is responsible for every part of the day.
journey.reaction: Who is responsible. That's the question I always ask and usually get a funny look for. Good to see it in the first few lines.

journey.quote: Compare quotes on the same guest count, spaces, hours, nights and currency before you pay any deposit.
journey.reaction: Before you pay any deposit. Sensible. My husband will like that it's put so plainly.

journey.quote: The Civil package includes a welcome drink, flowers and Greek desserts in the room on arrival, a bouquet and boutonniere of olive branches and seasonal white flowers, rice and petal baskets, a wedding cake, koufeta (sugared almonds) and a sparkling wine breakfast the morning after.
journey.reaction: On the iPad this whole section turns into one long string of bouquets and breakfasts in bed, hotel after hotel. That's my daughter's department. I started skimming here and nearly missed the useful bits about fees.

journey.section: Are Crete wedding packages all inclusive?
journey.quote: So treat a Crete package as the core of the day, and ask for every reception item as its own line.
journey.reaction: Thank you. I'd assumed 'all inclusive' meant the dinner too. That's exactly the kind of thing that blows a budget.

journey.section: What's left out or charged on top
journey.quote: Euphoria states that its packages are complete, its items are not interchangeable, and unused services carry no refund or alternative, though packages can be customised at extra cost.
journey.reaction: No refund for things you don't use. I'm glad someone told me before we paid for a jazz musician nobody wanted.

journey.quote: Elounda SA notes the Metropolis fee for an Orthodox wedding sits outside its package rate.
journey.reaction: Municipal fee, Metropolis fee. I'm not sure what the Metropolis is here. A church authority? A few plain words would help me explain it to my husband.

journey.quote: The Elounda SA brochure states that symbolic weddings and vow renewals are not legally recognised in Greece.
journey.reaction: That's important and I'm glad it's said straight. I wouldn't want them coming home thinking they're married when they're not.

journey.section: Venue package, venue fee or a planner
journey.quote: Whichever route you take, write down who is responsible for each part of the day.
journey.reaction: Yes. In writing. This page keeps coming back to that, and it's why I'm starting to trust it.

journey.section: East or west Crete for a package wedding
journey.quote: Think about where your guests will fly in, how long they will stay and whether one resort can hold everyone, then compare the packages within that corner.
journey.reaction: With Mum coming, the drive from the airport matters. I'd like to know how far the other resorts are, not just the one that's 15 minutes away.

journey.section: How to compare two Crete quotes like for like
journey.quote: **Deposits and cancellation.** Ask what the deposit secures, whether it is refundable, when the balance is due and what happens if you postpone.
journey.reaction: This is the one I lose sleep over. I'm circling it before I forward the list.

journey.section: How to compare two Crete quotes like for like
journey.quote: Nana Princess recommends evening ceremonies, because high-summer temperatures can reach 35 degrees C, with ceremonies from 6.30pm to 8pm in July and August.
journey.reaction: 35 degrees with my mother sitting in the sun? I'm glad this is here. Evening it is.

journey.section: How to compare two Crete quotes like for like
journey.quote: **Level access.** Can older guests reach the ceremony and reception without steps or sand, and is there an accessible bathroom nearby?
journey.reaction: Someone thought of Mum and her walking frame. 'Or sand' too, with all these beach ceremonies. I'd still love to know which of these places actually pass that test.

journey.section: How to compare two Crete quotes like for like
journey.quote: **Contract language.** Is the contract in English, and which version applies if there is a Greek one too?
journey.reaction: That's exactly my worry and I've never seen anyone else raise it. Good.

journey.quote: How far could the exchange rate move the total between deposit and balance, and who carries that risk?
journey.reaction: My husband's question, word for word. Euros worry us both.

journey.quote: It notes that Greece is in an active seismic zone and that wildfires occur in the extended summer period from June to September.
journey.reaction: Honest without frightening me. Paired with the insurance question, it's what I'd want to check for the older relatives.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and confirms every inclusion in writing before you commit, so you can book a Wedded Concierge consultation whether you already hold quotes or are still shaping your shortlist.
journey.reaction: Australian dollars and everything in writing before we commit. That's most of what I want. A consultation sounds like I'd get to speak to a person.

unanswered_questions: Which of these Crete venues have step-free routes to the ceremony and reception for a guest with a walking frame?
How long is the drive from the airport to each resort, not just Grecotel Amirandes?
What exactly is the Metropolis fee, and who pays it?
Is the deposit protected in any way if a venue or supplier lets us down?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong on the day, at 2am Greek time?
Is the consultation a phone call with a named person before anything is booked or paid?

turn_offs_found.quote: The Civil package includes a welcome drink, flowers and Greek desserts in the room on arrival, a bouquet and boutonniere of olive branches and seasonal white flowers, rice and petal baskets, a wedding cake, koufeta (sugared almonds) and a sparkling wine breakfast the morning after.
turn_offs_found.why: Long run-on lists like this, one after another through the venue section, read as walls of text on my iPad. I lose the thread and almost skip the practical lines about fees and conditions hidden between them.

would_share_with: My husband, with the compare-quotes checklist printed and the deposit, currency, contract language and level access points circled
My sister, who will look after Mum on the trip, with the heat, seismic, wildfire and insurance lines
My daughter, with the 'all inclusive' section, so she knows the reception is usually extra

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and confirms every inclusion in writing before you commit, so you can book a Wedded Concierge consultation whether you already hold quotes or are still shaping your shortlist.
cta_reaction.why: AUD quotes and everything in writing tick my main boxes. I'd click if I knew the consultation is a phone call with a real, named person, before anything is paid, who can tell me which venues suit my mother.

top_3_changes: Break the long inclusion sentences in the venue-by-venue section (Out of the Blue Civil, Minoa Palace, Elounda Lavish, Euphoria tiers) into short bullet lists so they don't read as walls of text on an iPad.
Give the Municipal and Metropolis fees a few plain words of explanation where they first appear.
Give each venue a one-line takeaway (conditions, rooms, coordinator) so a careful reader doesn't lose the thread before reaching the checklist.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, practical, reads top to bottom on an iPad)
No invented brand facts; missing business details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments, image slots and VERIFY markers treated as invisible
Title, deferred business details, sourcing and absent prices not raised as must-fix, per orchestrator
Journey types limited to the allowed enum; every turn-off has a why

open_questions.question: No blockers for this persona. Remaining asks are readability (long inclusion lists, plain-English fee terms) and are should-fix at most. Deposit protection, on-the-day contact and a phone-first consultation are business details and deferred.

assumptions: Margaret reads the whole article on an iPad because her daughter sent it, and her own mother uses a walking frame (per voice samples).
Prices are deliberately not printed, so their absence was not raised.
